extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for oaths, declarations, and related data (inventorship, signatures, venue, seals, translations, supplemental oaths) in U.S. patent applications, including continuation/divisional practice and examiner handling guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staleness of Oath/Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will no longer require a newly executed oath or declaration based on an oath or declaration being stale (i.e., when the date of execution is more than 3 months prior to the filing date of the application) or where the date of execution has been omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are reminded that they have a continuing duty of disclosure under 37 CFR 1.56.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Prior Oath/Declaration in Continuation/Divisional (37 CFR 1.63(d)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (other than a continuation-in-part) may be filed with a copy of the oath or declaration from the prior nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy may be submitted even if it identifies the prior application number. If the copy is filed after the continuation/divisional's filing date and an application number has been assigned, the cover letter accompanying the copy should identify the continuation/divisional application number and indicate the copy is from a prior application to avoid incorrect matching. The copy itself should be labeled with the continuation/divisional application number in case the cover letter is separated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of Prior Oath When Specification Differs (No New Matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the oath or declaration from a prior nonprovisional application may be filed in a continuation or divisional even if the continuation/divisional specification differs (revisions to clarify text or incorporate amendments), provided the changes do not constitute new matter relative to the prior application (see 37 CFR 1.52(c)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner determines the continuation/divisional contains new matter relative to the prior application, the examiner should notify applicant in the next Office action, require a new oath or declaration with the surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f), and indicate the application should be redesignated as a continuation-in-part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation/Divisional of Application with 1.47 Status
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional of a prior application accorded status under 37 CFR 1.47 will be accorded status under 37 CFR 1.47 if a copy of the decision according status under 1.47 in the prior application is filed in the continuation/divisional, unless an oath or declaration signed by all inventors is included upon filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because an oath/declaration in an application accorded 1.47 status generally is not signed by all inventors, if a copy submitted omits signatures of one or more inventors, OPAP should send a 'Notice to File Missing Parts' requiring the missing signature(s), unless a copy of the 1.47 decision is included at filing. Reply options to the Notice include filing a copy of the 1.47 decision together with the late-filing surcharge under 37 CFR 1.16(f) or submitting an oath or declaration signed by the previously nonsigning inventor with the surcharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Prior Applicant Named Inventor Is Not an Inventor in Continuation/Divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inventor named in a prior application is not an inventor in a continuation or divisional filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), the continuation/divisional may be filed either (A) with a copy of an oath or declaration from the prior application and a statement requesting deletion of the person(s) not inventors (see 37 CFR 1.63(d)), or (B) with a newly executed oath or declaration naming the correct inventive entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d), the request for filing must be accompanied by a statement requesting deletion of the non-inventor(s) (see 37 CFR 1.53(d)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing When Petition to Add an Inventor Was Filed (37 CFR 1.48)
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation/divisional of a prior application in which a petition under 37 CFR 1.48 to add an inventor was filed should be filed with either a copy of the executed declaration naming the correct inventive entity from the prior application or a newly executed declaration naming the correct inventive entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of any decision under 37 CFR 1.48 from the prior application is not required to be filed in the continuation/divisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of Oath/Declaration (37 CFR 1.69)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an individual making an oath or declaration cannot understand English, the oath or declaration must be in a language that such individual can understand and shall state that such individual understands the content of any documents to which the oath/declaration relates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the text of any non-English oath/declaration is in a form provided by the PTO or in accordance with PCT Rule 4.17(iv), it must be accompanied by an English translation together with a statement that the translation is accurate. Exception: for an oath/declaration filed under § 1.63, the translation may be filed in the Office no later than two months from the date applicant is notified to file the translation. The Office will accept a single non-English oath where joint inventors only some understand English but all understand the non-English language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Oath or Declaration Permitted/Required (37 CFR 1.67)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require, or inventors/applicants may submit, a supplemental oath or declaration meeting the requirements of § 1.63 or § 1.162 to correct deficiencies or inaccuracies in an earlier filed oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.67 requires substantially all data called for in 1.63. A supplemental oath cannot be used to introduce new matter into an application. In proper situations the supplemental oath may be made on information and belief by an applicant other than the inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Must Sign Supplemental Oath (37 CFR 1.67(a)(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Deficiencies/inaccuracies relating to all inventors/applicants may be corrected with a supplemental oath signed by all inventors/applicants; deficiencies relating to fewer than all may be corrected with a supplemental oath identifying the entire inventive entity but signed only by the inventor(s)/applicant(s) to whom the error or deficiency relates; deficiencies due to failure to meet 1.63(c) may be corrected with an application data sheet under 37 CFR 1.76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of a supplemental oath or application data sheet is governed by 37 CFR 1.33(a)(2) and paragraph (b) of § 1.67. Examples (1–4) illustrate common corrective situations (citizenship error, omitted duty-to-disclose clause, deceased inventor corrected by legal representative, mailing address correction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Oath Required for Newly Presented Claims or Improper References to New Matter (37 CFR 1.67(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental oath meeting 1.63 must be filed when a claim is presented for matter originally shown or described but not substantially embraced in the originally presented statement of invention or claims, or when an oath/declaration submitted under 1.53(f) after filing improperly refers to an amendment that includes new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No new matter may be introduced into a nonprovisional application after its filing date even if a supplemental oath/declaration is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling When an Inventor Refuses or Cannot Be Found (37 CFR 1.183 reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an inventor who executed the original declaration refuses or cannot be found to execute a required supplemental declaration, the requirement for that inventor to sign may be suspended or waived in accordance with 37 CFR 1.183.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All available joint inventors must sign the supplemental declaration on behalf of themselves, if appropriate, and on behalf of the nonsigning inventor (see MPEP § 409.03(a)). If there are no joint inventors, the party with sufficient proprietary interest must sign on behalf of the nonsigning inventor (see MPEP § 409.03(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 6.06 — New Oath for Subject Matter Not Originally Claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental/new oath or declaration is required when the application presents a claim for subject matter not originally claimed or embraced in the statement of the invention (use form paragraph 6.06).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new oath/declaration must properly identify the application (preferably by application number and filing date) in the body. Examiner note: Explain the new claimed matter in bracket 1; brief summary of the invention must be commensurate with the claimed invention and may need modification (see MPEP §§ 608.01(d) and 1302, and 37 CFR 1.73).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Oath or Declaration Filed After Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental oaths/declarations covering claims have been filed after allowance as a matter of right and when received will be placed in the file by the Office of Data Management, but their receipt will not be acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such filings should not be considered amendments under 37 CFR 1.312 since they make no change in the wording of the papers on file (see MPEP § 714.16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who May Administer Oaths (37 CFR 1.66)
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath or affirmation may be made before any person within the United States authorized by law to administer oaths. An oath made in a foreign country may be made before any diplomatic or consular officer of the United States authorized to administer oaths, or before any officer with official seal authorized to administer oaths in the foreign country, whose authority shall be proved by a certificate of a U.S. diplomatic/consular officer or by an apostille.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The oath must be attested by the proper official seal. The oath is valid as to execution if it complies with the laws of the state or country where made. When the person administering lacks a seal, official character must be established by competent evidence (certificate from a clerk of court or similar). See MPEP § 602.04(a) for foreign executed oath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Declarations vs Oaths and Notary Seal Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents with seals cannot be adequately scanned for retention in an Image File Wrapper; the Office strongly encourages use of declarations rather than oaths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the person before whom the oath is made lacks a seal, the examiner should require proof of authority. Seals may be embossed or rubber stamped; do not confuse a stamped legend indicating only the date of expiration of the notary’s commission with an official seal. In some jurisdictions the notary seal is not required but the official title must be on the oath (list of states given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue Requirement for Oath
rubrics_metrics.description: The venue (portion indicating where the oath is taken) must show that the oath was taken within the jurisdiction of the certifying officer or notary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the county and state in the venue agree with the county and state in the seal no problem arises. If venue and seal do not correspond, the jurisdiction must be determined from statements by the notary. Otherwise, require a new oath/declaration or a certificate by the officer stating the oath was executed within his/her jurisdiction. Form paragraph 6.07 may be used when venue is not shown; where seal and venue differ use 'Notice of Informal Application' form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notarial Powers of Military Officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain military officers on active duty have general powers of a notary public and consul of the U.S. when executing notarial acts outside the continental U.S. (list: judge advocates, law specialists, summary courts-martial, adjutants, commanding officers of Navy/Coast Guard, staff judge advocates, and others designated by regulations/statute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The signature without seal of such a person acting as notary, together with the title of his/her office, shall be prima facie evidence of his/her authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consular Authentication and Hague Convention/Apostille
rubrics_metrics.description: When an oath is made in a foreign country not a member of the Hague Convention, the authority of an officer other than a U.S. diplomatic/consular officer must be proved by certificate of a U.S. diplomatic/consular officer (see 37 CFR 1.66 and MPEP § 604).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the required authentication/certificate/apostille is omitted, the application is accepted for examination but the examiner should note the informality in the first Office action and require either (A) a new properly authenticated oath by an appropriate diplomatic/consular officer, (B) filing of a proper apostille, or (C) a declaration under 37 CFR 1.68. Form paragraph 6.08 may be used to notify applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney-in-Application Administering Oath
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney in the application is not barred from administering the oath as a notary if such practice is permissible under the law of the jurisdiction where the oath is administered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the law of the jurisdiction (e.g., District of Columbia) prohibits administering oaths by the attorney in the case and the oath is known to be void for that reason, require a new oath/declaration and refer the file to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant and Inventorship Definitions and Filing Consequences (37 CFR 1.41, 1.53)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent is applied for in the name(s) of the actual inventor(s). The inventorship of a nonprovisional application is that set forth in the oath/declaration filed to comply with 37 CFR 1.63, except as provided in 1.53(d)(4) and 1.63(d). The inventorship of a provisional application is that set forth in the cover sheet (37 CFR 1.51(c)(1)). If an oath/cover sheet is not filed, inventorship is that set forth in the application papers filed pursuant to 1.53(b)/(c), unless applicant files a paper with the processing fee supplying or changing inventor names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an application is filed without an oath/declaration, provide the name, residence, and citizenship of each person believed to be an actual inventor as an application identifier. If no inventor is known, provide an alphanumeric identifier (avoid very short identifiers). Failure to provide an identifier may result in inability to match subsequent papers with the application and possible need to resubmit time-dependent papers. For correction of inventorship see MPEP § 201.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Inventors Must Apply Jointly (37 CFR 1.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint inventors must apply for a patent jointly and each must make the required oath or declaration; neither one nor fewer than the entire number can apply for a patent for an invention invented by them jointly, except as provided in § 1.47.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventors may apply jointly even though they did not physically work together, made unequal contributions, or did not contribute to every claim. For nonprovisional applications each named inventor must have contributed to at least one claim; for provisional applications each named inventor must have contributed to the subject matter disclosed in the provisional. See 35 U.S.C. 116 concerning joint applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's Citizenship Requirement (35 U.S.C. 115)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute requires an applicant in a nonprovisional application to state his/her citizenship. A statement that the applicant is not a citizen of any country satisfies the requirement; statements about citizenship applied for or future citizenship do not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 6.05 and 6.05.03 may be used to notify applicant that citizenship is omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residence Requirement in Oath/Declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s place of residence (city and either state or foreign country) is required in the oath/declaration in a nonprovisional application for compliance with 37 CFR 1.63 unless included in an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76). For applicants in the U.S. Armed Services, a statement to that effect is sufficient as to residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If residence is omitted from the executed oath/declaration or application data sheet, OPAP will normally indicate the deficiency on a 'Notice of Informal Application' to require submission of residence information within a set reply period. Examiners should use form paragraphs 6.05 and 6.05.02 when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing/Post Office Address Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant’s mailing or post office address is required on the oath/declaration if not stated in an application data sheet; mailing address means the address where the applicant customarily receives mail (home or business acceptable) and should include ZIP code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The address of the attorney with instruction to send communications to applicant 'in care of' the attorney is not sufficient. For incomplete/omitted addresses on oaths filed prior to December 1, 1997, use form paragraph 6.09.01; otherwise use form paragraphs 6.05 and 6.05.19 or 6.05 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraphs for Oath/Declaration Defects (6.05 series)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the oath/declaration is defective, a new oath/declaration in compliance with 37 CFR 1.67(a) identifying the application by number and filing date is required; examiner should follow with one or more appropriate form paragraphs (6.05.01–6.05.20) describing the specific defect(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none of the specific form paragraphs apply, an appropriate explanation of the defect should be given immediately following the general 'oath or declaration defective' paragraph. Specific example paragraphs include 6.05.02 (residence omitted), 6.05.03 (citizenship omitted), 6.05.11 (notary signature missing or wrong place), 6.05.12 (notary seal and venue omitted), etc.
